texts: My sister can tell within minutes whether a salesman is honest or just smooth, and I want to learn that skill of separating real from fake.
doha on being able to tell the real from the fake
Give me a doha about the wise person who sifts every claim and every face, keeping what is real and letting the false drift away, the way a sharp mind separates genuine from counterfeit.
real from unreal
Two roads of words lie before the heart; the clear-eyed one parts the true from the glitter and walks on.
doha: washerman sorts clean from dirty, i wanna sort real from fake like that
washerman, real versus fake
The washerman parts the clean from the soiled by his eye; so let the wise part the true from the false.
A washerman near us sorts hundreds of bundles each morning without a single mistake, and I wish I could sort people and claims so surely; doha?
I'd like a doha showing that as the washerman separates the clean from the soiled with a glance, the discerning mind separates the real from the unreal, keeping the one and setting aside the other.

I'd like a doha for someone who keeps falling for smooth talkers, urging him to develop the sharp inner sense that tells real from unreal, the kind that quietly weighs every offer before it is believed.
I have been fooled by three flattering friends in a row, and I wish I had some inner sense that told me who is real.
doha pls: how to tell fake ppl from real ones
sifting real from false
Let the mind keep a quiet clarity, that the false may fall away and only the true remain.
one-string lute, discernment
On the one-string lute the singer hears the false note at once; so the wise ear parts the real from the empty.
A street singer with a one-string lute can tell in a second when a note is false, and I would love to have that sort of judgment about people.
Write a doha showing that as the singer of the one-string lute catches a false note instantly, the wise person catches the false word and false face, and keeps only what rings true.
doha w one-string lute: tell false notes from real ones in life
When two advisers told me opposite things, I had to quietly decide which was real, and it made me wish for a clear sense of judgment.
Craft a doha praising the quiet power that lets a person look at two things that seem the same and tell which is real and which is only appearance, without being swayed by the crowd.
real from unreal
doha on judging what is real
Where all things glitter, the clear-seeing part the true from the shine.
doha w heron + sun: looks pure but isnt, wise ppl can tell
A man in our lane looks as calm and white as a heron in the morning sun, but I have learned to see what hides behind such show; doha?
The heron stands in white beneath the sun, but the discerning eye sees what it stalks.
Please make a doha about the heron that looks pure and still in the bright sun, though it hunts, teaching the wise to look beyond a spotless appearance and tell the real from the pretended.
heron, sun, seeing through
The wise heart sifts and keeps the true; the foolish heart clutches all that glitters.
doha about knowing what to keep n what to throw away in life
I am clearing out my life after a long mess, deciding which friends, habits and beliefs are real and which only look good, and I want a doha for it.
Write a doha about the mind that can weigh every voice that comes to it, keeping the worthy, rejecting the false, and so walking through a noisy world with a calm, clear sense of what is real.
sifting true from false
river, crow, telling apart
The river runs clear and muddy together; the crow drinks anything, but the wise sip only the clean.
I need a doha showing that the river carries both clear and muddy flow, and the crow takes whatever comes, while the wise person chooses carefully what to take in and what to leave.
I used to believe everything I read online, like a crow pecking at anything, but now I treat information like a river and check what is clear and what is muddy.
doha w river n crow: choose carefully what u take in
A mark upon the brow proves nothing; the wise look past the sign to the soul.
doha: dont judge by the forehead mark, look deeper
forehead mark, looking deeper
Can you put together a doha about learning not to be impressed by the mark on a man's forehead or his holy appearance, but to look deeper and tell who is genuine and who only wears the signs.
A man in our neighborhood always has a fresh mark on his forehead and a pious manner, and I learned the hard way to look past such things.
The bee passes the husk and seeks the nectar; so the wise take the sweet and leave the empty.
bee, choosing the real
doha: bee picks only the good stuff, i wanna be like that
Write a doha about the bee that visits many blossoms but takes only the nectar, showing how a discerning mind passes over the useless and gathers only what is real and nourishing.
I read a hundred opinions on how to live, but like a bee I try to take only what is actually useful; maybe a doha on that.
My jeweler friend tested every claim on his touchstone and said the true philosopher's stone is the ability to tell real from false; I want a doha on that.
Test it on the touchstone, and the philosopher's stone itself must prove its worth; so the wise try every claim.
doha w philosopher's stone n touchstone: test everything b4 u believe
Give me a doha showing that even something said to be a philosopher's stone must be tried on the touchstone, and the wise test every claim before believing, so that only the real passes.
touchstone, philosopher's stone
ocean, sorting real from false
I'd like a doha about the vast ocean of voices and opinions in which a person can drown, advising that only clear judgment tells which is real and which is foam, and so keeps him steady.
The internet felt like an endless ocean of advice until I learned to tell which parts were real and which were only noise.
doha: ocean of opinions, how to sort the real ones
In the ocean of voices, the clear-eyed one finds what is real.
doha w churn: separate the butter from the rest like sorting real from fake

Write a doha showing that as the churn separates butter from the rest, a patient and discerning mind separates what is real from what is only froth, keeping the substance and discarding the remainder.
The churn turns, the butter rises; so the wise mind turns each matter until the real floats up.
churn, separating real
My aunt churns every morning and always knows the moment the butter has formed; I wish I could sense the right moment to separate fact from rumor like that.
pearl, real versus fake
My friend bought a pearl at a bargain price, and I could tell at a glance it was glass; people ask how I knew, and I want a doha on that sense.
doha: tell a real pearl from a fake one
Craft a doha about the keen eye that tells a real pearl from a glass imitation at one look, showing that the discerning person judges by what a thing is rather than how brightly it shines.
The pearl and the glass both gleam; only the clear eye knows which was born of the deep.
thief, needle, sharp judgment
I once spotted a thief pretending to be a customer because I noticed one tiny detail, as fine as the eye of a needle, and I want a doha on such sharpness.
The thief hides in honest clothes, but the sharp eye passes the needle of the real through the false.
doha w thief + needle: spotting liars with sharp eyes

Please make a doha about the sharp eye that sees through the thief's honest face, passing through the finest needle's gap of detail to tell the real from the pretended, and so protecting the household.
temple, telling true from false
A man who loudly gives at the temple gets everyone's respect in our town, but I look at how he treats his workers, and I think judgment should rest on that.
doha: dont judge by temple donations, see how they act
Not by the offerings at the temple but by the deeds of the day does the wise judge a soul.
Write a doha about the discerning person who looks beyond the show of devotion at the temple to the hidden conduct of a man, and judges his worth by what he does rather than what he displays.
doha: at a crossroads u gotta pick the real path not the flashy one
At the crossroads many voices call; the clear-eyed one walks the road that is real, not the one that glitters.
I need a doha about a person standing at the crossroads of a major decision, surrounded by tempting offers, who calmly separates the real from the showy and chooses wisely.
crossroads, choosing wisely
I am at a crossroads with two job offers, one that shines and one that is quietly right, and I would like a doha about telling them apart.
doha on wise judgment, tell good from bad
clear judgment
The sharp eye parts the true from the false as dawn parts the night from the day.
Please write a doha about the ability to look at a person, a promise or an idea and quickly see whether it is real or counterfeit, a gift that protects a person through all his life.
My grandmother never went to school but could tell in a minute who was honest, and I would love a doha about that kind of judgment.
After the village drought, my mother would sip from a pot of water, drop in a leaf, and judge by it whether it was safe, and I think of that careful sense.
pot of water, leaf, judging
Can you put together a doha about the wise person who knows by a single leaf floating in a pot of water whether the water is clean, a mind that reads small signs to tell real from false.
A single leaf upon the pot of water tells the careful eye what is clear and what is not.
doha w pot of water + leaf: reading small signs to judge
Write a doha for the one who needs to pick friends carefully, saying that real discernment is the quiet sense that separates the loyal from the merely pleasant and keeps one safe in the crowd.
choosing the genuine
Many smile at the gate; the wise one knows which smile is true.
After my business partner betrayed me, I finally understood the difference between those who flatter and those who are real.
doha on picking genuine friends over fake ones
chakor bird, moneylender, judgment
doha w chakor bird + moneylender: spotting the real deal from the fake
The chakor bird waits only for what is real, while the moneylender's smile is a price; the wise know the difference.
A moneylender offered me a friendly deal that sounded too sweet, and I remembered the loyalty of a chakor bird, and could finally tell what was real.

Give me a doha about how the chakor bird will not accept a substitute for what it longs for, while the moneylender's sweet words come with hidden cost, teaching the wise to separate genuine from calculated.
doha on knowing right from wrong clearly
I'd like a doha for the young about the quiet gift of seeing a thing as it truly is, without being fooled by its dress, a gift that grows with patience and keeps them from many a regret.
At the interview I could sense that the glowing description of the job was not matching the way people acted, and it saved me from a mistake.
seeing what's real
Dress and name may change a hundred times; the clear mind sees what lies beneath.
furnace, real versus fake
A smith told me he can tell real metal from false just by how it behaves in the furnace, and I wish people were so easy to read.
doha: furnace shows whats real, how to tell ppl apart
The furnace proves the metal; the wise mind proves every claim and keeps what survives.
Write a doha about how the furnace separates the real from the counterfeit, and how the wise person puts every claim and every character to some test so that only what is genuine remains.
A fine cloth sheet may hide a rough body; the wise look past the covering to what lies beneath.
A man in a beautifully clean cloth sheet came calling with a pious story, and my gut told me something was wrong, and it was.
Craft a doha showing that the clean cloth sheet one wears is no proof of a clean heart, and that the discerning person looks beneath the covering to tell the real from the pretended.
cloth sheet, seeing beneath
doha w cloth sheet: dont trust clothes, check the person
Please make a doha about the discerning listener who is not swayed by a smooth tongue, who listens to what is said and weighs it against what is done, and so is rarely deceived by sweet words.
The tongue may drip with honey; the wise ear weighs the deed behind it.
tongue, judging words
A smooth-talking coworker charmed everyone, but I noticed his words never matched his actions, and I would like a doha for the quiet watchful ones.
doha: dont trust sweet talk, check the actions
crow, oil press, judgment
The crow chatters; the oil press hums; the wise ear knows which is noise and which is yield.
doha w crow + oil press: tell noise from real work
In our village the crow's loud cawing and the oil press's steady hum fill the morning, and I learned to tell who in town is noisy and who actually works.
Write a doha about how the crow makes much noise and gives nothing, while the oil press works quietly and yields oil, teaching the wise to tell the loud from the productive.
doha: dont judge ppl by how often they go to the mosque, look at their deeds
Not by the prayers at the mosque but by the kindness of the hand is the true heart known.
I need a doha about the discerning mind that does not judge a man by how many times he is seen at the mosque, but by how he treats the hungry and the weak outside.
mosque, judging by deeds
Everyone in our neighborhood praises a man who is at the mosque five times a day, but I watched how he treated his workers and drew my own conclusion.
Can you put together a doha that says the sharpest eye is not the one that sees most but the one that tells real from unreal, and that such judgment outweighs any amount of information.
sharp judgment
Many see; few can tell the true from the shine.
doha on sharp judgment
I used to collect facts, but I only became wise when I learned to judge which ones were real and which were noise.
potter and clay, bell, judgment
The potter taps his work and hears the flaw; the bell rings true only if it is whole; the wise ear tells which is sound.
doha w potter and clay + bell: ear tells whats sound
A potter shaping clay taps his work and listens for the flaw, and a bell rings clear only when it is whole; I want a doha about that kind of sharp judgment.
Write a doha about the potter who works clay and listens to the ring of his work, like a bell that sounds true only when sound, teaching the wise to tell the real from the flawed by gentle testing.
ocean, bitter gourd, discernment
Give me a doha about how even the whole ocean cannot sweeten a bitter gourd, and how the wise person learns to see a thing's real nature and not be fooled by where it was bathed.
Though bathed in the ocean, the bitter gourd stays bitter; the clear eye knows the nature beneath the wash.
My relative made pilgrimage everywhere, as if bathing in the ocean, but remained as harsh as a bitter gourd, and it taught me to judge by nature and not by display.
doha w ocean + bitter gourd: judge a persons nature not their rituals
doha w lock: smart ppl know which key fits, i wanna judge right
lock, finding what fits
I tried several keys on the old lock, and watching how the right one slid in made me think of how real choices click when you see clearly.
I'd like a doha about the discerning person who knows at once which key fits which lock and which choice fits which need, because his clear mind sees what is real and what only looks like it fits.
Many keys glitter, but only one turns the lock; the clear-eyed know it by feel.
The furnace proves the metal, the ear proves the tongue; the wise mind keeps what survives the test.
A friend's sweet-tongued promise went through the furnace of a hard situation, and only then did I see which of his words were real.
doha w tongue + furnace: promises get tested by hard times
tongue, furnace, testing words
Write a doha about how a tongue can say anything, but the furnace of hardship proves which words were real, a lesson in the discerning habit of watching how people behave under heat.
furnace, physician, judgment
doha w furnace n physician: a good doctor can tell real from fake
The physician tests the fever, the furnace tests the metal; the wise test all things before trusting.
Craft a doha about the physician who tells a real illness from a pretended one at a glance, and the furnace that tells real metal from false, showing the value of trained judgment.
Our family physician can tell at once when someone is faking an illness, as a smith can read metal in the furnace, and I would love that kind of sharp judgment.
tree, judging by fruit
My grandfather used to say you know a tree by its fruit, not its shade, and that is how he judged people his whole life.
Judge the tree by its fruit, not its height; so the wise judge a soul by deeds.
doha: tree is known by its fruit, judge ppl by actions
Please make a doha showing that a tree is known by its fruit and not by its height or its bark, just as the discerning judge a man not by his claims but by what his life actually bears.
river, clear and muddy
doha w river: some flows clean, some muddy, learn to tell
The river carries clear and muddy together; the wise know which to drink.
Write a doha about the river that carries both clear and muddy flow in its course, teaching the wise to tell which source to trust and which to avoid, in people and ideas alike.
At the river I watched where the clear stream met the muddy one, and thought about how I should tell good influences from bad in my own life.
doha w temple + moth: dont get drawn to the shiny thing
My cousin gets drawn to every flashy new guru like a moth, and I keep telling him that real places like a true temple don't need to glitter; doha for him?
temple, moth, judgment
I need a doha about the moth that rushes to every bright thing and is burned, while the discerning visitor to a temple looks past the glitter to find what is truly sacred and steady.
The moth is drawn to the glitter; the wise one enters the temple's quiet and tells the real from the bright.
doha about choosing wisely between things that look alike

Please write a doha for a young person facing many tempting options, about the clear sense that separates what is lasting from what is only attractive, so that he does not spend his days chasing what fades.
I used to chase every shiny opportunity, and only after losing years did I learn to judge which ones were real.
lasting versus showy
Between the lasting and the showy, the wise choose the quiet and keep it.
The mind that tells the true from the false walks through a crowd as through an empty field.
doha about telling what is real
I could tell the moment my colleague began lying, just by something in how he spoke, and I want a doha about this inner radar.

Can you put together a doha about the keen inward sense that quietly tells a person which words are sincere and which are only polish, a sense that grows with attention and protects the one who has it.
inner judgment
The moneylender in our town is friendly and always smiling, but I learned to read his terms, not his smile, and that saved my family.
The moneylender's smile is wide and the contract narrow; the wise read the latter.

Write a doha about the discerning borrower who looks past the moneylender's friendly manner to the real terms, teaching that the sweetest voice is not always the safest and that careful judgment protects.
moneylender, reading carefully
doha w moneylender: dont trust the smile, read the terms
yogi, stone, true or false
The yogi sits as still as stone, but stillness is not always wisdom; the clear eye tells which is which.
A yogi in our area sits motionless like a stone and draws crowds, but I learned to ask what he actually knows, and not be impressed by stillness.
doha w yogi + stone: dont be fooled by looking calm
Give me a doha showing that a yogi may sit like a stone and impress the crowd, but the discerning person asks what lies behind the stillness, telling the genuinely wise from those who only appear so.
I want a doha about the person who can read a room and instantly tell who is sincere and who is acting, a quiet gift that comes from attention rather than cleverness and protects him all his life.
reading sincerity
In my first week at the new office, I could already tell who was real and who was posturing, and I would love a doha on that instinct.
Behind every mask, a quiet truth; the clear mind lifts the veil gently.
doha on spotting fake ppl
A cleric in our area gives impressive speeches, but I learned to ask who he actually helps, and the answer taught me how to judge.
doha: dont be fooled by a cleric's fancy speeches
cleric, judging by deeds
Grand is the cleric's speech, but the wise look at the hand that feeds the poor.
I'd like a doha about the discerning listener who does not judge a cleric by his fine speech or his title, but by what he actually does for the people around him, and so is never deceived.
dew, real versus fleeting
Dew shines like treasure at dawn and is gone by noon; the wise know which brightness lasts.
Write a doha about how dew shines like treasure at dawn but vanishes by noon, teaching the discerning mind to tell what is lasting from what only sparkles for a moment.
I almost invested everything in something that sparkled like dew in the morning, but judgment told me it would be gone by noon, and I stepped back.
doha w dew: shiny stuff doesnt last, learn to tell
Craft a doha about the thirsty person who tests a pot of water by its color and smell before drinking, showing how the wise do not swallow anything just because it is offered.
Before the thirsty lip touches the pot of water, the wise eye asks if it is clean.
On a long journey I was offered a pot of water by a stranger and checked it carefully before drinking, and later I thought of how we should check ideas the same way.
doha w pot of water: check before u drink it, same w ideas
pot of water, careful testing
sun, seeing clearly
Please make a doha about how the sun reveals the true colors of all things hidden in dim light, and how the discerning mind, like sunshine, shows what is real and what only seemed so in the dark.
Under the harsh afternoon sun I finally saw the real condition of the place I had been about to rent, and it taught me to look in clear light before deciding.
doha: the sun shows whats real, clear judgment
In the sun's full gaze the false loses its color, and the true stands plain.
palanquin, judging worth
A man arrived in a palanquin with great pomp, and many bowed, but I waited to see how he treated the bearers before forming my opinion.
The palanquin is gilded but the bearers are bent; the wise judge a man by his kindness to those who carry him.
Write a doha about the discerning observer who does not bow to the man in the palanquin until he sees how he treats those who carry him, judging worth by conduct and not by show.
doha w palanquin: dont judge ppl by their fancy ride
mosque, needle, judgment
I need a doha about the keen eye that passes like a needle of detail through the show at the mosque, telling the sincere worshipper from the one who performs, and judging by quiet signs and deeds.
At the mosque I could tell by the smallest detail, like the point of a needle, which of the men there were sincere and which were just performing; I want a doha on this.
The needle of the clear eye passes through the show at the mosque and finds the one who truly prays.
doha w mosque + needle: spotting sincere vs show
doha about choosing what is real over what looks good
I used to be impressed by anyone who looked successful, but life taught me to ask what is real underneath, and I want a doha about that change.
Appearance is a bright cover; the wise ask what lies behind.
separate real from fake
Can you put together a doha about the mature mind that no longer takes things at face value, that asks quietly what is real beneath what is shown, and so spends its days on what truly matters.
Write a doha about the cuckoo's sweet voice and the rope that binds, teaching that the discerning person listens to a pleasing voice yet checks whether a hidden cord of selfish intent is attached.
cuckoo, rope, careful judgment
A voice sweet as the cuckoo may hold a rope behind it; the wise listen and look.
A salesman with a sweet cuckoo-like voice almost got me to sign a contract that was a rope around my neck; I would like a doha on staying alert.
doha w cuckoo + rope: sweet voice can hide a trap
true versus false
I went through my old beliefs one by one, keeping those that held up and dropping the rest, and it felt like a spring cleaning of the mind.
doha: sorting what to believe and what to drop
Let the mind be a quiet judge, keeping the true and releasing the false without anger.
Give me a doha about the daily habit of examining each belief and each claim, keeping what is real and releasing what is false, until the mind is clear, light, and not easily fooled.
